performer.name: The Invitation
performer.stance: frazzled amateur organizer with a staple gun; talks fast, apologises a lot, keeps going anyway

structure: one week told in order, cards woven into her speech without labels: Wednesday flyers, Thursday doors, Saturday at the bench, Sunday notes, Monday's stripe, back to the two armchairs
synopsis: A spoken-word number from a card deck about protopia: the future as slow, small improvement people take part in. A performer tells how they organised a first small repair job in their street, from putting up flyers to the first Saturday.
bestOfReason: Night of the flyers 3, 1, 2, 17: the ugly flyer, the open page, pencil, and the performer's own card naming time, place, task.
Doors 26, 27, 13, 15, 28: the first hello, the door that stays shut, the badly dressed neighbour who knows how, going first.
Saturday 19, 5, 6, 18, 7, 8: the clumsy start, one fixable thing, a repair not a revolution, shared hands, a boring win that compounds.
Afterwards 9, 33, 34: one breath against the feed, your own notes, the honest count.
Sneaking it in 42, 43: the tiny pilot stripe, mild disobedience.
Price and close 46, 47, 55, 56: trading certainty for agency, showing up again, nobody claps, pick up the pencil.

omitted.10-12: body and attention cards; 9 carries the one breath
omitted.21-24: present-tense cards; the week itself is told in the present
omitted.48: refers to the other two decks' bargain
omitted.49-54: design-signature cards; 56 lands the pencil instead

orderReason: Cards follow one week in time instead of deck order: the flyer (3) before the idea on it (1, 2); the performer's own card (17) closes the flyer night; door cards (26, 27, 13, 15, 28) before the Saturday cards; 9 moves to the moment someone checks the news during the repair.

cues.cue: staple gun clacks on the backbeat
street noise, a bus pulls away

beats: Wednesday, eleven at night, one staple gun, two hundred flyers. If you walked home tonight, you've seen one. Sorry about your lamppost.
Every living room on this street has two armchairs. One says doom, one says saved. Both very comfortable. The third option has no chair. Some people call it protopia. I call it Saturday.

beats.pre: Yes, I made the flyer myself, and yes, it's ugly.
beats.text: Make the first version bad on purpose. Bad is how you know it is real.
the future is a process of slow, incremental improvement you participate in.
beats.post: Nobody reads small print. That's why I put the truth there.

beats.pre: Time and place in pencil, because
beats.text: pencil means you expect to be wrong and stay anyway.

beats.pre: And on top, in letters you can read from a bus:
beats.text: The Invitation. Turn watching into showing up. Name a time, a place, a task.
beats.post: Saturday, nine, the bench by the bus stop. Bring gloves.

beats.pre: First door, a prickly man. I said hi. You
beats.text: lower the bar to contact. Most cooperation starts embarrassingly small.
They might not respond. Your nervous system thinks that is death. It is not.

beats.pre: Third door, a wrench and a terrible hat.
beats.text: Authority is overrated, proximity is underrated. Ask the one who actually does the thing.
real know-how is often badly dressed and lives three doors down.

beats.pre: After that I knocked first everywhere.
beats.text: Go first. Every ally was a stranger until somebody did.

beats: Saturday, nine. Four of them came. Last time it was me and a thermos, so this is a movement.

beats.text: A pigeon, an emu, a duck and a crow huddled over a coffee carafe: the first small, clumsy gathering. Clumsy is the entry fee.

beats.pre: The bench has a loose slat, so that's our
beats.text: one broken thing close enough to touch.
A repair you can finish this week, not a revolution you can only announce.

beats.pre: Eight hands, one slat, and we
beats.text: split a problem the way your ancestors raised a barn.

beats.pre: Somebody checks the news. Phone down.
beats.text: Take the one breath the feed is built to deny you.

beats.pre: Done by ten. Nobody filmed it, because
beats.text: small fixes do not trend. They just hold.

beats.pre: Next week, the hinge on the hall.
beats.text: One repair a week is fifty-two a year. Nobody clapped, and the place is different.

beats: Sunday I wrote it all down.

beats.text: Write down what you actually saw, not what the headline said you would see.
Count the whole thing, including the times it worked and nobody noticed.

beats: Monday, the crossing by the school. Three years of petitions, no stripe.

beats.pre: There's a little white stripe there now. No idea who.
beats.text: Run a tiny version. Low stakes, real feedback, no permission needed.
improvement often looks like mild disobedience to a stuck system.
The Comfort of Maybe: trade the warm baths of hopeless and handled for the cold shower of it depends on us.
there is no final version. The cost is showing up again next week.
Nobody will clap. Start anyway. The clapping was never the point.
Forget the brochure. Ignore the loop. Pick up the pencil.

beats: Doom gets the subscriptions. Rescue gets the tickets. A Saturday with a loose slat earns nothing, which is how you know it's yours.
Same bench, next week, nine. Bring gloves.
